stem: You have renamed a resource block in your configuration from `resource "aws_s3_bucket" "data"` to `resource "aws_s3_bucket" "storage"`. Before running `terraform apply`, you need Terraform to update the tracked state address so it matches the new configuration identifier without destroying and recreating the live cloud bucket. Which command should you execute?
options: terraform state rm aws_s3_bucket.data && terraform state rm aws_s3_bucket.storage
objective: List tracked state addresses and rename or relocate resources in state using terraform state mv

stem: An EC2 instance managed by Terraform in production (`module.compute["prod"].aws_instance.web`) has experienced an operating system corruption and must be completely recreated on the next deployment. You are not allowed to edit any `.tf` configuration files. How should you plan this recreation?
options: Run terraform taint module.compute["prod"].aws_instance.web followed by terraform plan
objective: Plan resource recreation using the -replace flag without modifying configuration files

stem: An engineer runs `terraform state mv aws_instance.web aws_instance.web_app` to rename a resource binding. A team member asks whether this command creates a backup file and whether backup creation can be turned off with a CLI flag. What is the correct answer?
options: Backup creation on terraform state mv can be disabled by supplying the -no-backup flag.
Terraform automatically writes a backup file on every state-modifying command, and this backup behavior cannot be disabled.
A backup file is only created if the Terraform state file is managed in a remote backend.
Terraform only creates backup files for read-only subcommands like terraform state list, so terraform state mv creates none.
objective: List tracked state addresses and rename or relocate resources in state using terraform state mv
